title: Weekly Cohort Retention Percentages
description:
For each signup-week cohort, compute the **percent of that cohort active** in week 0, 1, 2, … after signup. `retention_pct = active_users / cohort_size * 100`, rounded to 2 decimals.

**Tables:** `users` (`user_id`, `signup_date`), `activity` (`user_id`, `active_date`)

Output columns: `cohort_week`, `weeks_since_signup`, `cohort_size`, `active_users`, `retention_pct`. Order by `cohort_week`, `weeks_since_signup`.
solution_sql: WITH cohorts AS (SELECT user_id, DATE_TRUNC('week', signup_date)::DATE AS cohort_week FROM users), sizes AS (SELECT cohort_week, COUNT(*) AS cohort_size FROM cohorts GROUP BY cohort_week), activity_w AS (SELECT a.user_id, c.cohort_week, (DATE_TRUNC('week', a.active_date)::DATE - c.cohort_week) / 7 AS weeks_since_signup FROM activity a JOIN cohorts c ON c.user_id = a.user_id) SELECT s.cohort_week, w.weeks_since_signup, s.cohort_size, COUNT(DISTINCT w.user_id) AS active_users, ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT w.user_id)::NUMERIC / s.cohort_size * 100, 2) AS retention_pct FROM sizes s JOIN activity_w w ON w.cohort_week = s.cohort_week WHERE w.weeks_since_signup >= 0 GROUP BY s.cohort_week, w.weeks_since_signup, s.cohort_size ORDER BY s.cohort_week, w.weeks_since_signup
hints: DATE_TRUNC('week', ...) aligns both signup and activity to Monday week starts.
Divide distinct active users by the pre-aggregated cohort_size, not by a running count.
explanation: Cohort week 2026-01-05 has 3 users: all active week 0, 2 in week 1 (66.67%), 1 in week 2 (33.33%). Cohort 2026-01-12 has 2 users: 100% then 50%. Retention tables always normalize by original cohort size so later weeks do not look artificially high.
